description: Make the .gitignore that gship init delivers actually ignore the .env family, and lock it with a durable git check-ignore test

userStories.title: Ignore the .env family in the template gitignore and lock it with a real git check-ignore test
userStories.description: As a user who runs gship init and then follows the product docs that tell me to put GITHUB_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN and RESEND_API_KEY in a .env at the project root, I need the .gitignore that init delivers to actually make git ignore that file and its local variants, so that agents running with bypassPermissions that commit and push on their own cannot carry my credentials to a public remote.
acceptanceCriteria: The .gitignore that gship init delivers makes git ignore a .env file at the root of the user's project, proven by behavior (real git check-ignore in a temporary repo fed with templates/.gitignore), never by substring presence. [oracle: bash -c 'T=$(mktemp -d); git -C $T init -q; cp templates/.gitignore $T/.gitignore; : > $T/.env; git -C $T check-ignore -q .env; rc=$?; rm -rf $T; exit $rc']

The same guarantee holds for the local-variant family, so the rule written is generic rather than two literal lines: .env.local, .env.production.local and .env.test.local are all ignored. [oracle: bash -c 'T=$(mktemp -d); git -C $T init -q; cp templates/.gitignore $T/.gitignore; m=0; for f in .env.local .env.production.local .env.test.local; do : > $T/$f; git -C $T check-ignore -q $f || m=1; done; rm -rf $T; exit $m']

A durable test named 'templates gitignore ignores dotenv' exists and passes, exercising real git check-ignore (not substring assertions) against the materialized project so a future removal of the protection is caught by the gate instead of by manual audit. [oracle: bash -c "bun test -t 'templates gitignore ignores dotenv' 2>&1 | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && bun test -t 'templates gitignore ignores dotenv' 2>&1 | grep -q '0 fail'"]

The durable test covers BOTH gitignore-production paths of materializeTemplates in the same run: the verbatim-write path (target project has no .gitignore) and the merge path (target project already has its own .gitignore), each verified with real git check-ignore over .env, .env.local, .env.production.local and .env.test.local. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The embedded copy that actually reaches the user carries the same protection: the .env rules are present in templatesContents['.gitignore'] inside src/vendor/_generated.ts. [oracle: bash -c "grep -q '\\\\n\\.env\\\\n' src/vendor/_generated.ts"]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
userStories.notes:
Files: templates/.gitignore (add the dotenv block), src/vendor/_generated.ts (regenerated, never hand-edited: run `bun run embed-vendor` then verify `bun run embed-vendor:check`), and ONE new test file, e.g. test/templates-gitignore-dotenv.test.ts.

Why a NEW test file and not test/embedded.test.ts: that file sits at 665 lines against a 666-line ceiling in scripts/file-size-budget.json, so appending a describe block there forces a ceiling raise plus a tracker-ref edit of the `_ref` prose field. A dedicated file avoids that entirely. src/vendor/_generated.ts stores each template as a single escaped string literal, so adding lines to templates/.gitignore does NOT grow its line count (50/51) and needs no ceiling raise.

Rule shape (the AC2 oracle exists to force this): `.env` alone does not cover `.env.local`, and `.env.*.local` does not cover `.env.local` either (the `*` cannot match empty between the two dots). The cam-cli root .gitignore lines 22-26 are the precedent to mirror: `.env`, `.env.development.local`, `.env.test.local`, `.env.production.local`, `.env.local`. Prefer the generic family form `.env`, `.env.*.local`, `.env.local` (the positive control the issue already ran), and do NOT use a blanket `.env*`, which would also ignore a `.env.example` a downstream project legitimately commits. Add a short comment header above the block in the template, matching the existing commented style of that file.

Test name: `bun test -t` matches the concatenated describe + test name, so wrap the cases in `describe('templates gitignore ignores dotenv', ...)` for AC3's oracle to match. Bun's default reporter emits no per-test line, hence the 'N pass' + '0 fail' oracle form (measured in CAM-497); do not rewrite that oracle to grep '^(pass)'.

Dual-path coverage (AC4): drive `materializeTemplates(cwd)` from src/templates/embedded.ts into a real tmpdir with `git init`, once with no pre-existing .gitignore (verbatim path) and once with a pre-existing user .gitignore such as `node_modules\n` (mergeGitignore path, which appends only missing non-comment lines). Then run real `git check-ignore -q <file>` per path via Bun.spawn / Bun.$ against files touched in that tmpdir. Hit real I/O at the wire boundary; no mock of git, no assertion that only checks substring presence.

Gotchas: (a) cam dual-copy is per-file, so confirm by running embed-vendor whether the template edit requires the embedded regen rather than assuming either way; (b) do NOT try to verify by running `gship init` in a tmpdir: it is interactive, opens tmux panes and hangs a non-interactive shell (timed out at 2 minutes on 2026-08-04); verify through template contents plus git check-ignore, exactly as the oracles do; (c) scope is deliberately narrow: do not add the other 18 runtime-artifact patterns missing from the template, and do not touch docs/launch-readiness.md.

Patterns consulted (scripts/cam/patterns.md): 'Agent-prompt self-hosting pattern' (templates/ is source of truth, regen after edit), 'Durable marker module template + a gitignore-coverage gap' (grep BOTH .gitignore and templates/.gitignore before assuming coverage), 'Seeding a new templates/scripts/cam/<file>' (embed-vendor can push a file past its size ceiling). scripts/cam/pattern-records.jsonl does not exist in this tree, so no fingerprint id is cited.
